title: Galilee of the nations (Matthew 4:12–25)
hookLine: a great light for a people sitting in darkness, by the sea road
tomorrow: who reaches him first when he comes down the mountain?

cards: Every town has a road where the streetlights go out first and get fixed last. Nobody holds a launch party there, and nobody posts the photos. So where does a light start?

John the Baptist has been thrown into prison, and Jesus doesn't head for Jerusalem, the city of the temple. He leaves Nazareth and settles in Capernaum, a town "upon the sea coast," a place of boats and nets.

teach.b: Matthew hears the prophet Isaiah in that move: "Galilee of the Gentiles; The people which sat in darkness saw great light." In Isaiah's own chapter, the King James says Galilee of the nations: the peoples beyond Israel.
Isaiah's words belong first to the Hebrew Bible, which Jews read as their own scripture.
Then Jesus begins to preach, "Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand," and calls two fishermen at their nets: "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."
So the answer to today's question: in Matthew, the light starts on a shoreline, among working people, in a place a prophet called the shadow of death. Light is shared ground with a neighbor.

teach.h: THE QUR'AN: ALLAH IS THE LIGHT.
teach.b: The Qur'an says, in Pickthall's translation: "Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth."
Muslims and Christians both reach for light to speak of God reaching people in the dark.

And one honest difference: Matthew sees the light dawn in a person, Jesus, who in John's Gospel says, "I am the light of the world." In the Qur'an, the Light is God's alone, and Jesus is honored as a messenger of God.
Two traditions, one image, each in its own words.

how: Isaiah's line about the people who walked in darkness seeing a great light is read in some churches at Christmas, and Matthew's version is read by some in the season after Epiphany.

games.q: what does “galilee of the nations” mean?
o: a desert where prophets went to fast
a royal city where the temple stood
a borderland where Isaiah saw a great light

games.q: galilee of the nations — tap the pairs.
p: Allah is the Light of the heavens

s: in Matthew, Jesus begins his preaching in Jerusalem
he settles in Capernaum, by the sea in Galilee, and begins there.
only Christians speak of God as light
the Qur'an says: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth (24:35, Pickthall).
Galilee of the Gentiles and Galilee of the nations name the same place
Matthew's King James says Gentiles, Isaiah's says nations: the same promise.

games.q: a new kid sits at the far end of the lunch table, where nobody looks. if you follow Matthew's map, where does the light start?
o: at the far end, with the kid nobody looks at.
at the popular end, so it spreads faster.
with your own friends first; maybe later.
games.why: in Matthew, the light doesn't start at the temple or the palace. it starts by the sea road, with a people sitting in darkness.

practice: Turn on one lamp, or face the brightest window, and look at the light for a few breaths.
Then let one neglected place come to mind, a street, a care home, a neighbor's door, a corner of your own life left dark, and hold the light and that place together until the sit ends.

wordCard.voice: Galilee of the nations. Isaiah's name for the land by the sea where, Matthew says, a people in darkness saw great light.

orig.note: Greek: Galilee. Matthew 4:15 calls it Galilee of the Gentiles, the nations.

carryVoice: Here's your line: light by the sea, and in Matthew it starts among the fishing boats. Until tomorrow.
